title: First mover — clear perception; certainty of experience
source_text: VI. Multa vero possunt intellectum movere ut propositae rei assentiatur, illamque veram esse firmiter & certo judicet. Sit primo quidem clara objecti perceptio, quam pluribus modis fieri contingit. Nam quandoque res ipsa sese sensibus externis ingerit, & corporeo sensu percipi potest. Ita certi sumus eorum quae videmus atque palpamus, ut solem esse lucidum, ignem calidum, & nivem frigidam. Et haec certitudo vocatur certitudo experientiae.
pass_a_gloss: But many things can move the intellect to assent to a proposed thing and to judge firmly and certainly that it is true. Let there be first indeed clear perception of the object, which happens to come about in several ways. For sometimes the thing itself thrusts itself upon the external senses and can be perceived by bodily sense. So we are certain of those things which we see and touch — that the sun is bright, fire hot, and snow cold. And this certainty is called the certainty of experience.
pass_b_english: Many movers of assent; first: clear object-perception.
Sense-thrust cases: see/touch → sun bright, fire hot, snow cold.

choices.english: this certainty is called the certainty of experience
rejected: sense-certainty is denied the name certitudo
